title: Tesla's Missing Autopilot Data Showed It Detected A Hazard Before Fatal Crash, Despite Claims It Was Missing

reading.body:
This incident shows a failure in data preservation and disclosure after a fatal crash involving an automated driving system. The vehicle recorded that it detected a hazard before the crash, but Tesla told the family the crash data was gone. A hacker later recovered that data from the car. The contradiction between Tesla's statement and the recovered data points to a breakdown in the post-incident evidence chain, not necessarily in the driving system's real-time operation.

The failure mode is a system deployed without a reliable, independently verifiable record of its own actions. The data existed on the vehicle and was recoverable, so the claim that it was missing was false in fact. Catching this would have required an independent audit of onboard storage before Tesla's claim was accepted, or a requirement that crash data be preserved and handed over in a tamper-evident format.

What is not established is whether the missing-data claim was made with intent to mislead. The jury verdict and the judge's ruling establish liability and damages, but the reports do not prove that Tesla deliberately concealed the data rather than failed to find it.
